overview: This 603-page file traces Japanese fishing and research vessels across the North Pacific from 1930 to 1938. Correspondence, patrol reports, legal memoranda, and vessel records document Alaskan port visits, Bering Sea fisheries, fur-seal research, and disputes over salmon. Later records follow Japanese fishing ventures in Panama and Costa Rica and concerns about Panama Canal security.
interest: Interdepartmental correspondence reveals how fisheries cooperation, commercial competition, and security concerns shaped U.S. responses to Japanese vessels.
